answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any switch of primary vendor risks delivery disruption during onboarding that the organization cannot absorb right now—memory_c2's positive switching experience doesn't establish how it would perform under this specific time pressure and volume constraint. Renewing flat also leaves the 18% cost mandate unaddressed. memory_c4 indicates that benchmarking-driven renegotiation at renewal previously recovered real margin on both price and payment terms without disrupting the relationship, and memory_c1/c6 corroborate that continuing with the incumbent preserves integration stability and can still yield volume-based cost improvements. Negotiating terms at this renewal point captures cost reduction pressure while keeping the proven, stable supply chain intact—directly serving the objective of lowering TCO without raising delivery risk. I'm verifying memory_c4 specifically because it's the load-bearing memory for this action's expected payoff, and switching vendor or adding a second source remain live options for the next review cycle once onboarding risk under current volume constraints can be properly assessed.
